title: Async dequant & prefill/decoding overlap for packed INT8 attention kernels
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Goal: implement and validate an asynchronous dequantization pipeline and scheduling changes that let packed INT8/FP8-friendly matmul & attention kernels overlap prefill and decode phases to reduce end-to-end latency and KV cache memory overhead for trimmed quantized models. Motivation: current runtime serializes dequant+compute during prefill which increases decode tail latency and doubles working set when we materialize FP16 buffers. We want to: 1) add an "async dequant" stage that streams dequantized tiles to compute while keeping KV stored in compact int8 representation; 2) introduce tiled attention kernels that directly consume int8 KV where possible; 3) extend kernel selection heuristics to prefer packed-int8 paths when sequence length and activation statistics indicate safe signal-to-quantization-noise ratio. Success metrics: 5-15% p95 latency reduction on medium-length sequences (128-512) and 10-30% reduction in GPU memory related to KV storage for int8-backed sessions.
background: We already have kernels for INT8/FP8 mixed paths (see ENG-8275, ENG-9432) but dequantization is currently executed synchronously before compute. For large prefill batches the additional copying and temporary FP16 buffers increase both latency and GPU memory peak. Some hardware (A100/H100) has good INT8 tensor core support but our kernel chooser defaults to FP16 for safety. Experiments from local bench/branch 'quant-tiling-experiments' show that per-channel scales + clipped calibration reduces outliers for attention keys by ~0.6 perplexity delta on a small eval set. This ticket is the integration and scheduler work required to safely enable the fast path in production.
notes: Design constraints and considerations: - Per-channel vs per-tensor scale trade-off: per-channel improves accuracy but increases metadata overhead; we'll keep per-channel for KV/write-heavy workloads. - Calibration cost: we'll run a lightweight 1-2 batch calibration at model load for customer-pinned models; for general-hosted we can use offline stored calibrations. - Fallback policy: runtime must fall back to FP16 when observed clip-rate > threshold or when dynamic range exceeds quantizer limits. - Safety nets: add latency & quality gates in rollout (canary followed by ramp), automatic rollback on quality regression. - Interaction with caching: prefix/KV caching needs to understand that stored keys are int8; cache snapshots must version quant params.
benchmarks: local-gpu:A100-48GB - baseline FP16 prefill p95=82ms; int8-async tiled p95=71ms (2026-03-12)
ci/quant-smoke - accuracy delta on eval-set: +0.4% ppl (acceptable) (2026-03-13)
work_log: 2026-03-10 - Created ticket. Initial spike: implemented prototype streaming dequant pipeline in branch 'feature/async-dequant'. Observed ~8-12% latency improvement for synthetic ops with tiled matmul.

2026-03-11 - Experimented with per-channel quantization for KV. Found ~0.5% lower accuracy degradation vs per-tensor; metadata overhead measured ~3% additional memory. Decided to use per-channel by default for large models.

2026-03-12 - Benchmarked on A100: prefill-step latency reduced from 82ms -> 71ms for sequence=256, batch=4. Spike: one workload showed a 1.6x increase in dequant CPU-side copy time; found source in synchronous memcpy in CUDA stream 0.
2026-03-13 - Implemented proper CUDA stream placement and pinned host buffers to eliminate CPU-to-GPU stall. p95 improved further to 67ms in isolated runs.

2026-03-14 - Started integration tests in staging; added automatic fallback threshold logic based on clip-rate and per-layer activation histogram. Open questions remain around rollout gating and metrics to monitor quality drift in hosted multi-tenant environment.
